title: Explicit dual pairing of a bounded finite-projective cochain complex
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $P^\bullet$ an integer cochain complex [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], zero outside $[a,b]$ for integers $a\le b$, whose terms are finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Define $D^n=\operatorname{Hom}_A(P^{-n},A)$ and $d_D^n(\phi)=(-1)^{n+1}\phi\circ d_P^{-n-1}$. This is a cochain complex, zero outside $[-b,-a]$, with finitely generated projective terms. For the direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and the unit complex $A[0]$, there are chain maps $\epsilon:D\otimes_A P\to A[0]$ and $\eta:A[0]\to P\otimes_A D$: $\epsilon$ on $D^{-n}\otimes_A P^n$ is $\phi\otimes x\mapsto\phi(x)$, and the degree-zero component of $\eta(1)$ in $P^n\otimes_A\operatorname{Hom}_A(P^n,A)$ is the tensor corresponding to $\operatorname{id}_{P^n}$ under $P^n\otimes_A\operatorname{Hom}_A(P^n,A)\cong\operatorname{End}_A(P^n)$. All other components are zero. These maps satisfy $(1_P\otimes\epsilon)\circ(\eta\otimes1_P)=1_P$ and $(\epsilon\otimes1_D)\circ(1_D\otimes\eta)=1_D$, with the canonical associators and unitors.

proof.text: For each integer n, set D^n=Hom_A(P^{-n},A). Since P^m=0 for m outside [a,b], D^n=0 for n outside [-b,-a]. For n in this interval, P^{-n} is finitely generated projective, so the finite-projective module dual-pairing node gives that D^n is finitely generated projective. Thus D has the asserted support and termwise finiteness/projectivity.

source.place: Tag 0FNK, lemma-left-dual-complex, converse: define N^n=Hom_R(M^{-n},R) and use the finite-projective module lemma

proof.text: The displayed differential squares to zero. For φ∈D^n, the composite d_D^{n+1}d_D^n is multiplication by (-1)^{n+2}(-1)^{n+1}=-1 followed by precomposition with d_P^{-n-1}d_P^{-n-2}, which is zero because P is a cochain complex. Hence (D,d_D) is a cochain complex.

source.place: Tag 0FNK, lemma-left-dual-complex, differential calculation following equation involving d_M and d_N

proof.text: Define ε on the total tensor by evaluation on the degree-zero summands D^{-n}⊗_A P^n and by zero on all other total degrees. For a homogeneous φ∈D^{-n}=Hom_A(P^n,A) and x∈P^{n-1}, the total differential of φ⊗x is d_D^{-n}φ⊗x+(-1)^{-n}φ⊗d_P^{n-1}x, and ε sends it to (-1)^{1-n}φ(d_P^{n-1}x)+(-1)^nφ(d_P^{n-1}x)=0. Since A[0] is zero outside degree 0, ε is a chain map to A[0]. Define η(1)=Σ_n c_n, where c_n∈P^n⊗_A D^{-n} is the tensor corresponding to id_{P^n} under the isomorphism of the finite-projective module dual-pairing node; the sum is finite by the bounds. Write c_n=Σ_k y_k⊗ψ_k and c_{n+1}=Σ_j z_j⊗χ_j. The two triangle identities of that node, evaluated on elements, say Σ_kψ_k(x)y_k=x for x∈P^n, Σ_jχ_j(z)z_j=z for z∈P^{n+1}, and φ=Σ_kφ(y_k)ψ_k for φ∈Hom_A(P^n,A). The component of dη(1) in total degree 1 lying in P^{n+1}⊗_A D^{-n} is (d_P^n⊗1)c_n+(-1)^{n+1}(1⊗d_D^{-n-1})c_{n+1}, by the signed differential of the tensor-complex definition. Since d_D^{-n-1}χ=(-1)^nχ∘d_P^n, we get (1⊗d_D^{-n-1})c_{n+1}=(-1)^nΣ_j z_j⊗χ_j∘d_P^n=(-1)^nΣ_jΣ_kχ_j(d_P^ny_k)z_j⊗ψ_k=(-1)^nΣ_k d_P^ny_k⊗ψ_k=(-1)^n(d_P^n⊗1)c_n, using φ=Σ_kφ(y_k)ψ_k for φ=χ_j∘d_P^n and then Σ_jχ_j(z)z_j=z for z=d_P^ny_k. Hence the component is (1+(-1)^{2n+1})(d_P^n⊗1)c_n=0 for every n, so dη(1)=0 and η:A[0]→P⊗_A D is a chain map. No use of d_P^2=0 is needed here; the relation is Stacks' displayed equation in the proof of 0FNK.

source.place: Tag 0FNK, lemma-left-dual-complex, converse and its proof: η is a finite sum, is a map of complexes, and the displayed differential relation proves the sign rule

proof.text: On each homogeneous summand P^n, the composite (1_P⊗ε)∘(η⊗1_P) uses only c_n and the evaluation on D^{-n}⊗P^n, hence is the first triangle identity of the finite-projective module dual-pairing node. On each D^{-n}, the composite (ε⊗1_D)∘(1_D⊗η) similarly reduces to its second triangle identity. All mixed-degree summands vanish because ε is zero away from total degree zero. The maps 1_P⊗ε, η⊗1_P, ε⊗1_D and 1_D⊗η are tensor products of degree-zero chain maps and the associator of total complexes is defined without signs (Stacks, More on Algebra, the list preceding 0FNJ), so no Koszul sign enters. Reassembling the homogeneous components with the canonical associators and unitors gives the two asserted chain identities.

source.place: Tag 0FNK, lemma-left-dual-complex, converse: read the construction backwards from the two module dual triangle identities

proof.text: If P is the zero complex or a single-term complex, the same formulas reduce respectively to the zero pairing or the ordinary finite-projective module pairing; the finite sum and support assertions remain valid. Therefore no endpoint or empty-support case introduces an additional hypothesis.
